title: Do places differ more than chance would make them?

y.name: Applications a year per 10,000 people (log scale)

views.label: Standard patents
views.subtitle: Standard patents: each area's applications a year per 10,000 people, against its population. Chance alone would keep 95% of areas between the dashed lines; 6.7% are above and 68.2% below.
views.note: 1,165 areas with no applications cannot be drawn on the log scale.

views.label: Trade marks
views.subtitle: Trade marks: each area's applications a year per 10,000 people, against its population. Chance alone would keep 95% of areas between the dashed lines; 15.0% are above and 71.4% below.
views.note: 329 areas with no applications cannot be drawn on the log scale.

views.label: Standard patents, pooled into SA3s
views.subtitle: Standard patents, pooled into SA3s: each area's applications a year per 10,000 people, against its population. Chance alone would keep 95% of areas between the dashed lines; 15.5% are above and 72.5% below.
views.note: 7 areas with no applications cannot be drawn on the log scale.

source: IP RAPID, FY2017 to FY2026; ABS Census 2021 (lens: regions). A funnel plot.
